words.definition: sleeping with your eyes closed and body resting
words.definitionVi: đang ngủ, nhắm mắt nghỉ ngơi
words.hint: The cat is asleep on the warm sofa.
words.fact: Most children need about ten hours of sleep.
sentences: The baby is asleep in bed.
Ben looks asleep on the sofa.
Please be quiet — Dad is asleep.
Ana falls asleep after the story.
My cat is asleep in the sun.
Don’t wake him; he is asleep.
I was asleep at nine o’clock.
Grandpa is asleep in his chair.

words.definition: your mum or dad's sister in your family
words.definitionVi: cô, dì — chị em của bố hoặc mẹ
words.hint: Your aunt might give you birthday presents.
words.fact: Some aunts live far away and visit on holidays.

words.definition: not sleeping; your eyes are open
words.definitionVi: không ngủ; mắt bạn đang mở
words.hint: An alarm clock helps you stay awake for school.
words.fact: Birds are awake and singing early in the morning.
sentences: I was awake at six o’clock.
Why are you awake so late?

words.definition: the numbers and street name where someone lives
words.definitionVi: địa chỉ nhà, số nhà và tên đường
words.hint: Write your address on a letter so it reaches home.
words.fact: Every house has its own special address.
sentences: Mum puts the address on the letter.
Our address is on this card.
The teacher asks for my address.
We learn our address at school.

words.definition: feeling scared or worried about something
words.definitionVi: sợ hãi, lo lắng về điều gì đó
words.hint: It is okay to feel afraid during a loud storm.
words.fact: Talking to a grown-up can help fear feel smaller.
sentences: I feel afraid of the dark.
Don’t be afraid of the dog.
Are you afraid of loud noises?
I’m not afraid of the water.
words.imageCredit: Neda Andel ~SLooK4U Blog ~ slowly coming back · CC BY-SA 2.0 · flickr · https://www.flickr.com/photos/31730451@N03/20371250443

words.definition: how many years old a person or thing is
words.definitionVi: tuổi, bao nhiêu năm tuổi
words.hint: You blow out candles for each year of your age.
words.fact: Turtles can live to a very old age — over 100 years!
sentences: Sam is the same age as me.
Write your age on the paper.
Children of all ages can play.
At my age, I go to bed early.
How old is she? What age?

words.definition: every one or every part of something
words.definitionVi: Tất cả; mọi phần của cái gì đó.
words.hint: All the children put their hands up together.
words.fact: When you finish all your homework, you feel proud.
sentences: Please put all the books away.
Mum buys fruit for all of us.
All my friends came to the party.
Do you want all the stickers?

words.definition: feeling okay and not hurt or upset
words.definitionVi: ổn, không sao, không bị thương
words.hint: After a small fall, ask "Are you all right?"
words.fact: Saying "I am all right" tells people you feel fine.
sentences: I’m all right after the fall.

words.definition: every time; at all times
words.definitionVi: Luôn luôn; mọi lúc.
words.hint: The sun always rises in the morning.
words.fact: Kind friends always help when you need them.
sentences: We always play in the park.
I always write in my book.

words.definition: a small program on a phone or tablet
words.definitionVi: ứng dụng trên điện thoại hoặc máy tính bảng
words.hint: You tap an icon to open a game app.
words.fact: Some apps teach you maths while you play.
sentences: I use an app at home.
Please open the app on your phone.
We learn with an app at school.
Noah takes a photo with an app.
We talk about an app in class.

words.definition: the part of your body behind your chest
words.definitionVi: phần cơ thể phía sau ngực của bạn
words.hint: Carry your backpack on your back.
words.fact: Your spine runs down the middle of your back.
sentences: I carry my bag on my back.
The cat sits on my back!

words.definition: not good; wrong or unpleasant
words.definitionVi: xấu, không tốt, tệ
words.hint: Eating too much candy is bad for your teeth.
words.fact: Everyone has a bad day sometimes — tomorrow can be better.
sentences: Don’t be bad to your sister.
Eating too much sweets is bad.

words.definition: in a wrong or poor way, not well done
words.definitionVi: một cách tệ, không tốt
words.hint: If you feel bad, tell a teacher or parent.
words.fact: Practising again can fix something done badly.
sentences: We played badly in the park.
Lily can run, but badly today.
I write badly when I’m tired.
He sings badly, but he tries!

words.definition: a place outside a window where you can stand or sit
words.definitionVi: một nơi bên ngoài cửa sổ nơi bạn có thể đứng hoặc ngồi
words.hint: You can stand on a balcony and look at the street.
words.fact: Some balconies have flowers in colourful pots.
sentences: There is a balcony in my house.
We have a balcony at home.
Can you see a balcony in the picture?
We eat breakfast on the balcony.

words.definition: a group of people who play music together
words.definitionVi: ban nhạc, nhóm chơi nhạc cùng nhau
words.hint: A band might have drums, guitar and singers.
words.fact: School bands sometimes play at concerts.
sentences: My brother is in a band.
Zoe plays the guitar in a band.
Can you see the band on stage?
We watch a band at the party.

words.definition: a room under a house, below the ground floor
words.definitionVi: một căn phòng dưới một ngôi nhà, dưới tầng trệt
words.hint: Some families keep old toys in the basement.
words.fact: Basements are cool in summer because they are below ground.
sentences: There is a basement in my house.
We have a basement at home.
Can you see a basement in the picture?
Our toys are in the basement.
words.imageCredit: Radzki, D.; Negri, A.; Kusiak, A.; Obuchowski, M. · CC BY 4.0 · wikimedia · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=157741091

words.definition: a small flying animal that sleeps upside down
words.definitionVi: con dơi, động vật bay ban đêm
words.hint: Bats come out at night to hunt insects.
words.fact: Bats use sound to find their way in the dark.
sentences: I can see a bat at the zoo.
The bat is at the zoo.
Can you draw a bat, please?
Ana has a book about a bat.
We learn about a bat at school.
Mia points to a bat in the picture.
My favourite animal is a bat.

words.definition: to have a name that people use for you
words.definitionVi: được gọi là, có tên là
words.hint: I am called Mia — that is my name.
words.fact: Every person in the world is called something different.
sentences: I am called Sam at school.
He likes to be called Leo.
The street is called Park Road.

words.definition: hair that grows on a man's chin and cheeks
words.definitionVi: râu, lông mọc trên cằm và má
words.hint: Some grandpas have long white beards.
words.fact: Beards grow slowly — just a little each day.
sentences: The clown has a red beard.

words.definition: better than all the others; number one
words.definitionVi: tốt nhất, số một
words.hint: Try your best even when something is hard.
words.fact: Your best friend is the person you trust most.
sentences: She draws best in our class.

words.definition: nicer or improved compared with before or with another
words.definitionVi: Tốt hơn; khá hơn trước hoặc hơn cái khác.
words.hint: Rest and water help you feel better when sick.
words.fact: Practice makes your drawing skills get better.
sentences: This story is better than that one.
You look better with a smile!

words.definition: a warm cover you put on a bed at night
words.definitionVi: chăn ấm phủ lên giường
words.hint: Pull the blanket up when you feel cold.
words.fact: A soft blanket can make bedtime feel cosy.
sentences: There is a blanket in my house.
We have a blanket at home.
Can you see a blanket in the picture?
I put a blanket on my bed.

words.definition: having light yellow or golden hair
words.definitionVi: có mái tóc màu vàng nhạt hoặc vàng
words.hint: Many people in northern countries have blonde hair.
words.fact: Hair colour can change a little in the sun.
sentences: Who has blond hair in class?
I want blonde hair in the play.

words.definition: not interesting; making you want to sleep
words.definitionVi: nhàm chán, không thú vị
words.hint: A long wait with nothing to do feels boring.
words.fact: Finding a fun game can turn boring time into fun.
sentences: I think maths is boring today.

words.definition: a container with a narrow top for drinks
words.definitionVi: chai đựng nước hoặc đồ uống
words.hint: Take a water bottle to school on hot days.
words.fact: Reusable bottles help reduce plastic waste.
sentences: There is a bottle in my house.
We have a bottle at home.
Can you see a bottle in the picture?
There is water in my bottle.
Mum buys a bottle of juice.

words.definition: the lowest part of something, not the top
words.definitionVi: phần dưới cùng, đáy
words.hint: Your shoes go at the bottom of the cupboard.
words.fact: Fish often swim near the bottom of a lake.
sentences: My bag is at the bottom.
Look at the bottom of the page.
Write your name at the bottom.
The toys are at the bottom.
Don’t sit at the bottom of the stairs.
There is mud on the bottom of my shoe.
Open the box from the bottom.
Who is at the bottom of the list?
The fish swims near the bottom.
Put the book at the bottom.

words.definition: a round deep dish for soup, cereal or fruit
words.definitionVi: cái bát, tô đựng thức ăn
words.hint: Pour milk into your cereal bowl at breakfast.
words.fact: Bowls are easier to hold than flat plates.
sentences: There is a bowl in my house.
Leo eats cereal from a bowl.
We have a bowl at home.
Can you see a bowl in the picture?
There is fruit in my bowl.

words.definition: not afraid to try something difficult or scary
words.definitionVi: dũng cảm, không sợ thử việc khó
words.hint: It is brave to speak in front of the class.
words.fact: Even brave people feel nervous sometimes.
sentences: Ana is brave about the dark.
This story has a brave hero.

words.definition: a short rest time between lessons or work
words.definitionVi: giờ nghỉ giữa các tiết học
words.hint: Play outside during the school break.
words.fact: A break helps your brain feel fresh again.
sentences: We have a break after maths.
What do you do in the break?
Leo walks in the playground at break.
The break is my favourite time.
We eat fruit in the break.

words.definition: very good or very clever
words.definitionVi: rất tốt hoặc rất thông minh
words.hint: The sun is brilliant on a clear summer day.
words.fact: Teachers say "brilliant!" when you do great work.
sentences: Zoe looks brilliant in that dress.
My friend is brilliant at art.
Why is this game so brilliant?
Smile — you did a brilliant job!

words.definition: to carry something to a place or person
words.definitionVi: mang, đem cái gì đến chỗ nào
words.hint: Bring your homework book to school tomorrow.
words.fact: Dogs can bring a ball back when you throw it.
sentences: Please bring your book to school.
Can you bring this for me, please?
My teacher asked us to bring pencils.

words.definition: to make something by putting parts together
words.definitionVi: xây dựng, ghép các phần lại với nhau
words.hint: You can build a tower with wooden blocks.
words.fact: Beavers build homes called dams from sticks.
sentences: I can build a house with blocks.
Can you build a bridge for me?
Do you build with Lego at home?
My teacher asked us to build a model.

words.definition: a place with walls and a roof, like a school
words.definitionVi: tòa nhà, công trình có tường và mái
words.hint: Look up — tall buildings have many windows.
words.fact: The tallest buildings in cities touch the clouds.
sentences: We go to that building on Saturday.
There is a big building near my house.
Can we go to the building, please?
I can see the building in the picture.
We learn about the building at school.

words.definition: a place where many buses stop and start
words.definitionVi: bến xe buýt, nơi xe buýt đậu
words.hint: Check the timetable at the bus station.
words.fact: Big cities have busy bus stations with lots of routes.
sentences: We wait at the bus station.
Sam likes the busy bus station.
Look at the big bus station!
We see the bus station near town.
Can you find the bus station?
Don’t run in the bus station.
My dad works at the bus station.
The bus station is next to the shop.
We travel from the bus station.

words.definition: a place on the street where a bus picks you up
words.definitionVi: trạm dừng xe buýt trên đường
words.hint: Wait quietly at the bus stop for your bus.
words.fact: Bus stops often have a sign showing the route number.
sentences: I wait at the bus stop.
We see the bus stop in the street.
Can you find the bus stop?
Don’t run near the bus stop.
My dad waits at the bus stop.
The bus stop is next to the park.
We get on the bus at the bus stop.

words.definition: having lots to do with no free time
words.definitionVi: bận rộn, có nhiều việc phải làm
words.hint: The shop is busy on Saturday mornings.
words.fact: Bees are always busy collecting nectar from flowers.
sentences: Mum is busy in the kitchen.
We are busy before the party.
words.imageCredit: Free Clip Art · CC BY-SA 4.0 · wikimedia · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=71788742

words.definition: to pay money to get something from a shop
words.definitionVi: mua, trả tiền lấy hàng
words.hint: You need money to buy snacks at the shop.
words.fact: Some people buy things online with a computer.
sentences: I can buy milk at the shop.
Sam can buy tickets very well.
Can you buy this for me, please?
Do you buy sweets at home?
My teacher asked us to buy pencils.

words.definition: a box with bars for keeping a bird or small pet
words.definitionVi: một hộp có thanh để nuôi chim hoặc thú cưng nhỏ
words.hint: Birds and hamsters live in cages.
words.fact: Cages keep small pets safe indoors.
sentences: There is a cage in my house.
We have a cage at home.
Can you see the cage in the picture?
My bird lives in a cage.
Mum buys a cage for the pet.
words.imageCredit: Morland, Valère Alphonse (en 1846), illustrateur · CC CC0 1.0 · wikimedia · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=132093279

words.definition: to phone someone or shout their name loudly
words.definitionVi: gọi điện hoặc gọi to tên ai
words.hint: Call your friend to invite them to play.
words.fact: Before mobile phones, people used house telephones to call.
sentences: I can call Mum at school.
Zoe likes to call her grandma.
Can you call him for me, please?
Do you call your friends at home?
My teacher asked us to call our parents.

words.definition: an area where people leave their cars
words.definitionVi: bãi đỗ xe, chỗ để ô tô
words.hint: Find an empty space in the car park.
words.fact: Some car parks are underground beneath buildings.
sentences: Dad leaves the car in the car park.
Tom likes the big car park.
We see the car park near the shop.
Can you find the car park?
Don’t run in the car park.
My dad parks in the car park.
We walk from the car park to school.

words.definition: thinking about danger so you do not get hurt or make mistakes
words.definitionVi: Cẩn thận, chú ý để không bị đau hoặc làm sai.
words.hint: Be careful when you cross the road.
words.fact: Careful drivers always look both ways first.
sentences: Emma looks careful with the glass.
Be careful when you cross the road.
We are careful near the water.

words.definition: in a slow safe way, without rushing or breaking things
words.definitionVi: một cách cẩn thận, chậm và an toàn
words.hint: Carry the glass jar carefully so it does not fall.
words.fact: Scientists work carefully when they do experiments.
sentences: We play carefully in the park.
I write carefully in my book.

words.definition: to hold something and take it somewhere
words.definitionVi: mang, cầm và đưa đi chỗ khác
words.hint: Carry your lunch box in your school bag.
words.fact: Ants can carry things heavier than their own body.
sentences: I can carry my bag at school.
Mia likes to carry the kitten.
Can you carry this for me, please?
Do you carry your lunch at home?
My teacher asked us to carry the books.

words.definition: a shiny disc that holds music or computer information
words.definitionVi: Đĩa sáng bóng chứa nhạc hoặc dữ liệu máy tính.
words.hint: Old music players read songs from a CD.
words.fact: CD stands for compact disc.
sentences: I use a CD at home.
Please put a CD on the table.
We learn with a CD at school.
We talk about a CD in class.

words.definition: the middle part of something, not the edges
words.definitionVi: phần giữa của một cái gì đó, không phải các cạnh
words.hint: The sports centre has a swimming pool inside.
words.fact: British spelling uses centre; American uses center.

There is a big shopping centre near my house.
Can we go to the sports centre, please?
Ben draws a star in the centre.
I can see the centre of the circle.
Don’t stand in the centre of the road.
Meet me at the centre of the park.
The ball is in the centre.
We write our names in the centre.

words.definition: to make something different or become different
words.definitionVi: thay đổi, làm cho khác đi
words.hint: Change your clothes after playing in the mud.
words.fact: Leaves change colour in autumn before they fall.
sentences: I can change my clothes at school.
We change our shoes every day.
Can you change this for me, please?
Do you change money at home?
My teacher asked us to change partners.

words.definition: a yellow or white food made from milk
words.definitionVi: phô mai, làm từ sữa bò
words.hint: Cheese melts on hot pizza.
words.fact: There are hundreds of different types of cheese.
sentences: We buy cheese at the shop.
Can you see cheese in the picture?
Mum puts cheese on the table.

words.definition: a building where you watch films on a big screen
words.definitionVi: rạp chiếu phim
words.hint: Buy popcorn when you go to the cinema.
words.fact: The first cinemas showed silent black-and-white films.

There is a big cinema near my house.
Can we go to the cinema, please?
Mia watches a film at the cinema.
I can see the cinema in the picture.
We talk about the cinema at school.

words.definition: a round flat shape like a ring or a wheel
words.definitionVi: hình tròn, như vòng tròn
words.hint: Draw a circle by going round and round.
words.fact: A pizza is often cut into triangle slices from a circle.
sentences: I draw a circle at school.
Noah has a circle on his paper.
We need a circle for the picture.
Zoe draws with a circle stencil.
Don’t forget to draw a circle.
Put a circle round the answer.

words.definitionVi: một chương trình vui nhộn với những chú hề, động vật và những tiết mục thú vị
words.hint: Circus performers sometimes swing on a trapeze.
words.fact: Circuses used to travel from town to town in tents.
sentences: We go to the circus on Saturday.
There is a big circus near my house.
Can we go to the circus, please?
I can see the circus in the picture.
We talk about the circus at school.

words.definition: a large town with many buildings and people
words.definitionVi: thành phố lớn, nhiều nhà và người
words.hint: Cities have tall buildings and busy streets.
words.fact: Some of the biggest cities have millions of people.

There is a big city near my house.
Can we go to the city, please?
Sam plays in the city park.
I can see the city in the picture.
There are many cars in the city.
Meet me in the city tomorrow.

words.definitionVi: ở giữa cái gì đó, không phải bên cạnh hay cạnh
words.hint: Stand in the center of the circle in PE class.
words.fact: The center of a pizza is often the first bite people take.

Ana stands in the centre of the room.
There is a big tree in the centre of the park.

words.definition: quick at learning and good at solving problems
words.definitionVi: thông minh, học nhanh và giỏi
words.hint: A clever fox found a way into the hen house.
words.fact: Clever crows can use tools to get food.
sentences: Ben found a clever way to open the box.
This puzzle is for clever children.
Sam gave a clever answer in class.

words.definition: to go up something using your hands and feet
words.definitionVi: leo, trèo lên bằng tay và chân

words.definitionVi: Đám mây trắng hoặc xám trên bầu trời, có thể mang mưa.

words.definitionVi: trời nhiều mây, không nắng

words.definition: a funny performer with bright clothes and makeup
words.definitionVi: chú hề, người biểu diễn hài hước

sentences: Where is the clown at the party?
The clown helps at the show.

My favourite clown has a red nose.

words.definitionVi: áo khoác ấm mặc khi trời lạnh

We put a coat in the bag.

words.definitionVi: cà phê, đồ uống nóng của người lớn

words.definitionVi: không ấm áp; khi không khí hoặc một cái gì đó cảm thấy lạnh

words.definitionVi: truyện tranh hài hước

words.definitionVi: một cuốn sách mỏng với những hình ảnh hoạt hình kể một câu chuyện

words.definition: a person whose job is making food in a kitchen

words.fact: Eating well and sleeping help you stay well.
sentences: Lily is well after her cold.
My friend is very well today.
We all feel well after sleep.

words.definition: Covered with water; not dry.
words.definitionVi: Ướt, có nước, không khô.
words.hint: Grass is wet after rain.
words.fact: Wet paint signs warn you not to touch.
sentences: Emma looks wet from the rain.
Don’t sit on the wet chair.
The grass is wet after rain.

words.definition: A very big animal that lives in the sea.
words.definitionVi: Một loài động vật rất lớn sống ở biển.
words.hint: It spouts water from a blowhole.
words.fact: Blue whales are the largest animals ever.
sentences: I can see a whale in the sea.
The whale swims in deep water.
Can you draw a whale, please?
Ana has a book about a whale.
We learn about whales at school.
Don’t shout near the whale boat.
Tom points to a whale in the picture.
My favourite animal is a whale.

words.definition: At what time something happens.
words.definitionVi: Khi nào, lúc nào.
words.hint: When do we eat lunch?
words.fact: When is one of the five W question words.
sentences: Speak when it is your turn.
We play when we finish homework.
I write when I am at home.
Don’t go when it is dark.
Children learn when they play games.

words.definition: Moving air outside.
words.definitionVi: Gió — không khí chuyển động.
words.hint: Wind makes trees sway and kites fly.
words.fact: Strong wind can turn windmill blades.
sentences: Sam plays outside in the wind.
Look at the wind in the trees!
We talk about wind in class.
Don’t go out in a strong wind.
I wear a coat in cold wind.
The wind blows my hat off.

words.definition: With a lot of wind blowing.
words.definitionVi: Có gió mạnh, nhiều gió.
words.hint: Hold your hat on a windy day.
words.fact: Windy days are perfect for flying kites.
sentences: Noah’s hair looks windy and messy.
Don’t fly your kite on a very windy day.
Leo holds his hat on this windy day.
We stay inside on windy nights.
Close the window — it is windy!

words.definition: A job, or something you need to do.
words.definitionVi: Một công việc hoặc điều gì đó bạn cần làm.
words.hint: Homework is work you do at home.
words.fact: Many grown-ups go to work every weekday.
sentences: Emma’s dad goes to work every day.
The work at school is easy today.
We finished our work with a smile.
Noah drew his dad at work.
My work is on the table.
We learn a lot from hard work.
Say thank you for your help at work.

words.definition: The Earth and all the people and places on it.
words.definitionVi: Trái đất và tất cả mọi người và những nơi trên đó.
words.hint: People live all around the world.
words.fact: The world has oceans, mountains, and deserts.
sentences: There are many countries in the world.
Noah likes maps of the world.
Our world is big and beautiful.
Can we help the world, please?
I can see the world on this map.
Animals live all over the world.
The world is full of stories.
We learn about the world at school.

words.definition: Not as good as something else; more serious or less good.
words.definitionVi: Tệ hơn những thứ khác; không tốt bằng.
words.hint: A cold feels worse than a sniffle.
words.fact: Comparing helps you choose the better option.
sentences: This weather is worse than yesterday.
Sam’s score is worse than mine.
This story is worse than the first one.
The rain got worse in the afternoon.
My drawing is worse than yours.

words.definition: The least good; worse than all the others.
words.definitionVi: Điều tồi tệ nhất; tệ hơn tất cả những người khác.
words.hint: The worst score is the lowest one.
words.fact: Even the worst day can teach you something.
sentences: What is the worst day this week?
This story is the worst one.

words.definition: A word we use for polite offers and wishes.
words.definitionVi: Từ dùng để mời lịch sự hoặc nói điều mình muốn.
words.hint: Would you like some juice?
words.fact: Would is softer and politer than will.
sentences: We would like to play outside.
Ana would like a new book.
What would you like for lunch?
I would love to see the sea.

words.definition: Not correct; not right.
words.definitionVi: Không đúng; sai.
words.hint: Cross out the wrong answer and try again.
words.fact: Learning from wrong answers helps you improve.
sentences: Noah looks at the wrong page.
Leo is wrong about the party time.
This word is wrong in my sentence.
My friend chose the wrong bag.
We all get things wrong sometimes.
Smile — you had the wrong shoe!

words.definition: The day before today.
words.definitionVi: Hôm qua — ngày trước hôm nay.
words.hint: Yesterday is already in the past.
words.fact: You cannot change what happened yesterday.
sentences: We played in the park yesterday.
Listen — what happened yesterday in class?
I wrote in my book yesterday.
Don’t forget what we learned yesterday.
Can you tell me about yesterday?
Children learned a new song yesterday.
